# PolymerFTS 0.10.0

Changes since v0.9.1 include new SCFT and field-theoretic simulation capabilities,
numerical corrections, and wheel-based Python installation.

## Highlights

- A CPU-FFTW backend alongside CPU-MKL and CUDA, with a shared propagator
  computation layer and checkpoint-based memory reduction.
- Non-orthogonal cells, non-periodic boundaries, space-group reduced bases and
  CrysFFT acceleration. Continuous chains offer `rqm4`, `rk2` and `cn-adi2`;
  discrete chains use their dedicated propagator solver.
- Canonical SCFT thermodynamics: full and relative Helmholtz free energies,
  molecular chemical potentials, grand potentials and binary bulk coexistence
  calculations for incompressible blends.
- Custom Langevin integrators and observable callbacks, including extension state
  in checkpoints. Built-in methods are LM (the default) and Euler-Maruyama.
- Complex Langevin FTS and a browser simulation script builder, both beta.
- Bidirectional PSCF conversion, including preparation of PolymerFTS simulation scripts.
- Expanded numerical regression coverage for propagators, conservation, stress,
  structure functions, contour refinement, backend agreement and restart equivalence.

## Numerical results and simulation behavior

**L-FTS structure functions recorded by v0.9.1 were too small by the number of
monomer types.** Multiply those saved values by two for AB systems or three for
ABC systems to correct this normalization error when comparing saved data with
new runs.

SCFT results distinguish the relative and full canonical free energies.
`free_energy` is relative to the homogeneous state at the same composition.
Use `free_energy_absolute` for the full canonical free energy, composition derivatives
and canonical-to-grand-canonical transformations. The v0.9.1 SCFT log used the
field-theoretic Hamiltonian with its constant omitted; match energy conventions
before comparing its numbers with the new output. For phase coexistence, use the
reference-species quantities in
[Phase Equilibrium](https://github.com/yongdd/langevin-fts/blob/v0.10.0/docs/theory/PhaseEquilibrium.md).

L-FTS now retries a failed saddle solve with the same proposed fields and noise
by default. Exhausting the retries raises `SaddlePointError` and records failure
in `run_status.json`; failed steps contribute no measurements. Set
`saddle.failure_policy="resample"` to request noise resampling explicitly.

The [changelog](https://github.com/yongdd/langevin-fts/blob/v0.10.0/CHANGELOG.md)
contains further numerical corrections and dated development history.

## Installation

Follow the [installation guide](https://github.com/yongdd/langevin-fts/blob/v0.10.0/docs/getting-started/Installation.md)
to build a wheel for your environment and install it with pip. MKL and FFTW have
separate setup paths. Wheel builds require CMake 3.25.2+, a C++20 compiler,
spglib and LAPACKE, with at least one computational backend. CUDA builds also
require toolkit 12.2+. Python 3.11+ and NumPy 2+ are required; the supplied
Anaconda environment uses Python 3.14.

## Migrating v0.9.1 inputs

The following v0.9.1 parameter names have supported aliases:

| Previous name | Current name |
| --- | --- |
| `distinct_polymers` | `polymers` |
| `box_is_altering` | `relax_cell` |
| `scale_stress` | `stress_scale` |
| `blocks[].fraction` | `blocks[].monomer_fractions` |
| `recording.recording_period` | `recording.checkpoint_interval` |
| `recording.sf_computing_period` | `recording.sample_interval` |
| `recording.sf_recording_period` | `recording.statistics_save_interval` |

The previous names in this table remain accepted, but supplying both names for
the same setting raises an error.

Replace `reduce_gpu_memory_usage` with `reduce_memory` explicitly: the old key is
not an alias. The new memory-saving algorithm stores selected contour checkpoints
and recomputes intervening propagators.

ADAM has been removed. Inputs using `optimizer.name="adam"` must switch to the
Anderson-mixing configuration (`optimizer.name="am"`) documented in
[Parameters](https://github.com/yongdd/langevin-fts/blob/v0.10.0/docs/references/Parameters.md).

## Checkpoint migration

New checkpoints use format version 2 and retain full RNG state, previous noise,
auxiliary fields, pending measurements and custom integrator/callback state.

**v0.9.1 checkpoints are unversioned.** Loading one requires
`continue_run(path, allow_legacy=True)` and emits a warning: settings cannot be
verified and pending measurements cannot be recovered. Legacy files cannot restore
custom integrators or callbacks. Do not assume identical trajectories across releases.

v0.9.1 does not restore the complete state in new checkpoints; resume them with
v0.10.0. See
[Extensions](https://github.com/yongdd/langevin-fts/blob/v0.10.0/docs/internals/Extensions.md)
for custom methods, observables and restart contracts.

**Full changes:** https://github.com/yongdd/langevin-fts/compare/v0.9.1...v0.10.0
